clue.text: After the happy event, non-boarders appear to give work

indicators.note: the pupils come after the happy event, so their word follows in the answer

parts.note: a happy event is a euphemism for a baby being born
pupils who go home each night rather than boarding are day boys

explanation.surface: Once the baby has arrived, the pupils who live at home seem to hand in their homework.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a novel by Beryl Bainbridge about Scott's Antarctic expedition; 'work' means a literary work, not a task.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a Beryl Bainbridge novel, so it is a literary work.

clue.text: Title narcotics from Sylvester and Caldwell

definitions.text: Title narcotics from Sylvester and Caldwell

parts.words: Title narcotics from Sylvester and Caldwell
parts.note: the leaf in question figures in the titles of Joshua Sylvester's pamphlet against smoking and Erskine Caldwell's novel of the poor rural South

explanation.surface: Two authors seem to have drugs named in their titles.
explanation.walkthrough: Joshua Sylvester wrote 'Tobacco Battered and the Pipes Shattered'; Erskine Caldwell wrote 'Tobacco Road'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both book titles name the smoked leaf, so these are the title narcotics.

clue.text: Greenwich lady an unusual Bennett character

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of these words are set out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A woman from Greenwich is said to be a strange figure in an Arnold Bennett novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges GREENWICH LADY AN; the result is the hero of Arnold Bennett's novel 'Clayhanger'.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the title figure of Arnold Bennett's Potteries novel, so a character created by that author.

clue.text: Heracles' nephew who found taking part in Euripides tragedy a rejuvenating experience

definitions.text: Heracles' nephew who found taking part in Euripides tragedy a rejuvenating experience

parts.words: Heracles' nephew who found taking part in Euripides tragedy a rejuvenating experience
parts.note: in Euripides' play about the children of Heracles, the hero's elderly nephew and comrade is miraculously made young again to fight in battle

explanation.surface: An actor's relative found that appearing in a Greek tragedy took years off him.
explanation.walkthrough: In Euripides' 'Heracleidae' the aged nephew of Heracles has his youth restored for one day so he can defeat Eurystheus.
explanation.definitionFit: Myth names him as the son of Iphicles and charioteer of Heracles, hence his nephew.

clue.text: Doris Lessing featured a good one from a shambolic group of them

definitions.text: Doris Lessing featured a good one from a shambolic group of them

parts.words: Doris Lessing featured a good one from a shambolic group of them
parts.note: Lessing's novel about a chaotic squat of would-be revolutionaries has a 'good' member of the bomb-making band as its title figure

explanation.surface: A novelist wrote about the one decent member of a hopeless gang.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel is 'The Good Terrorist' (1985), about an inept London cell of militants.
explanation.definitionFit: The shambolic group in Lessing's novel are militants planting bombs, people using violence for political ends.

clue.text: Amy Lowell's colourful sort of mode

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to sort or rearrange, so the letters of the word mode are reordered

explanation.surface: An American poet's work is a vivid kind of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges MODE; Amy Lowell's first collection was 'A Dome of Many-Coloured Glass', so her colourful thing is a glass cupola.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowell's book title pictures a cupola of many-coloured glass, so her colourful one is that roof.

clue.text: Agreement given to wooden objects last night in ballad

parts.note: a word of agreement is yes
treen is a collective term for small household objects turned from wood

explanation.surface: Someone said yes to some woodwork the evening before, in a folk song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' simply joins the two parts. The answer is an old Scots word found in ballads such as 'Sir Patrick Spens'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an archaic Scots word meaning yesterday evening, typical of traditional ballads.

clue.text: Someone we both know in a Victorian novel

definitions.meaning: a person acquainted with you and me alike

explanation.surface: A mutual acquaintance turns up in a nineteenth-century book.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes a shared acquaintance and is also the title of Dickens's last finished book.

clue.text: His wife was liable to be choked off

definitions.text: His wife was liable to be choked off

parts.words: His wife was liable to be choked off
parts.note: in the Arabian Nights the ruler Shahryar married a new bride each day and had her killed next morning, so his wives risked strangling

explanation.surface: A husband whose wife might be throttled.
explanation.walkthrough: Shahryar of the 'Thousand and One Nights' killed each new wife until Scheherazade stopped him with her stories; 'choked off' plays on 'told off'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eastern monarch with a harem, whose wives might be strangled at his order.

clue.text: Spinner, perhaps, protects daughter by making textual changes

definitions.note: the definition describes the man by his activity: he is the one who made the cuts

indicators.note: the bowler protects the daughter by wrapping around her, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a spin bowler in cricket is one example of a bowler

explanation.surface: A cricketer shields his daughter while editing a text.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Bowdler produced a 'Family Shakespeare' with the rude bits removed; the clue defines him by what he did.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Bowdler expurgated Shakespeare, giving us the verb for censoring a text prudishly.

clue.text: French poet gets the wind up?

definitions.meaning: the cold north wind blowing down the Rhone valley

explanation.surface: A poet from France becomes alarmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the wind up' means becomes frightened; here 'gets ... up' merely joins two readings of one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic Mistral wrote in Provencal; the same name belongs to the fierce wind of southern France.

clue.text: "Literary men are all -s and charlatans" (Emerson)

parts.note: the missing word in Emerson's sentence pairs with charlatans: performers of tricks and illusions

explanation.surface: An American essayist dismisses writers as frauds.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in Emerson's line; the word sits naturally beside 'charlatans'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage magician deceives an audience, the same charge Emerson lays against writers beside charlatans.

clue.text: Art teacher's daughter who suffers at the rainbows end

definitions.text: Art teacher's daughter who suffers at the rainbows end

parts.words: Art teacher's daughter who suffers at the rainbows end
parts.note: in D H Lawrence's novel about the Brangwens, the daughter of Will, a craft and art teacher, endures illness and miscarriage before the closing vision of a rainbow

explanation.surface: A girl whose father teaches art suffers before finding the end of the rainbow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Rainbow' ends with its heroine ill and alone, then seeing a rainbow over the land.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the eldest Brangwen girl and heroine of Lawrence's novel, whose father becomes an art and handwork instructor.

clue.text: A stanza with connections to the Crown

definitions.text: A stanza with connections to the Crown

parts.words: A stanza with connections to the Crown
parts.note: the seven-line stanza known as rhyme royal is named for its use by a medieval poet and later a Scottish king

explanation.surface: A verse form that has links with royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme royal stanza of 'Troilus and Criseyde' is also called by this adjective; 'royal' is the link to the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme royal was introduced into English by the poet of the Canterbury Tales and bears his name as an alternative label.

clue.text: Paintings as stock market sector?

definitions.meaning: shares in petroleum companies, grouped as one sector

explanation.surface: Pictures considered as a category of shares.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paintings are called by this short word, which is also the market's term for petroleum stocks.

clue.text: They are in the hand of God, Solomon tells us, apocryphally

definitions.text: They are in the hand of God, Solomon tells us, apocryphally

parts.words: They are in the hand of God, Solomon tells us, apocryphally
parts.note: the Wisdom of Solomon, a book of the Apocrypha, says the souls of the just are held in God's hand

explanation.surface: A biblical king tells us who is in God's keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: Wisdom 3:1 begins 'But the souls of the ... are in the hand of God'; the book is in the Apocrypha, hence 'apocryphally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verse names the virtuous and just, those whose souls rest in God's hand.

clue.text: Mailer at pains to get subject matter

indicators.note: pains suggests the letters are put through torment and come out twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Norman Mailer takes trouble to find something to write about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pains' rearranges MAILER AT; 'to get' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer's raw stuff or subject matter is also called the substance he works with.

clue.text: The second Mrs Rochester

parts.note: Charlotte Bronte's governess heroine marries Mr Rochester after his first wife, Bertha, dies

explanation.surface: A man's second wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertha Mason is the first Mrs Rochester; the novel's narrator becomes the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The governess heroine of Bronte's novel marries Rochester once his first wife has died.

clue.text: Destination for Osbert Lancaster and Yeats

definitions.text: Destination for Osbert Lancaster and Yeats

parts.words: Destination for Osbert Lancaster and Yeats
parts.note: Yeats wrote a poem about sailing to the old city on the Bosphorus, and the cartoonist Lancaster wrote a travel book with a similar title

explanation.surface: Two writers headed for the same place.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeats's poem is 'Sailing to Byzantium'; Osbert Lancaster, cartoonist and writer, published 'Sailing to Byzantium: An Architectural Companion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both titles name the ancient city that became Constantinople as the place sailed to.

clue.text: Essayist's pseudonym might be a lie

indicators.note: might be hints that these letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer's pen-name could be a falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges A LIE to give the pen-name of Charles Lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb signed his Essays with this name, so it is an essayist's pseudonym.

clue.text: Dusty, ——' covered, maimed and set at nought" (Samuel Butler)

definitions.text: Dusty, ——' covered, maimed and set at nought" (Samuel Butler)

parts.words: Dusty, ——' covered, maimed and set at nought" (Samuel Butler)
parts.note: Butler's line pictures a neglected thing under dust and spiders' threads

explanation.surface: A Victorian writer describes something neglected and despised.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing word fits 'dusty' and a neglected object: a spider's silk covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A neglected object gathers dust and spider-silk, so it is covered in the spider's threads.

clue.text: Restore theatrical company, currently broadcasting

parts.note: a repertory company is called rep for short
something being broadcast right now is on air, so air stands for broadcasting

explanation.surface: Revive a theatre group that is on the radio at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On air' means being broadcast, so the clue's 'currently broadcasting' points to AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend or fix something is to restore it to working order.

clue.text: Valued at zero — still made speech

parts.note: O is the round figure for zero
something valued has been rated

explanation.surface: Graded at nothing, someone still gave a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Valued at zero' is RATED with O, and the O comes first; 'still' joins to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a formal address is to declaim or make a speech.

clue.text: Hill's Holy Week prayers

parts.note: Geoffrey Hill's 1978 collection takes its title from the Latin services of darkness held late in Holy Week

explanation.surface: Devotions for Easter week on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: Hill here is the poet Geoffrey Hill, not a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for darkness names the Holy Week offices of matins and lauds, and Hill's book.

clue.text: Articles on Scottish composer

parts.note: the definite article is the
the indefinite article is a

explanation.surface: Pieces written about a composer from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' gives two grammatical articles, one after the other; Thea Musgrave is a Scottish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thea Musgrave, born in Edinburgh, wrote operas such as 'Mary, Queen of Scots'.

clue.text: Witty, like Thackeray's snobbish author

definitions.meaning: Thackeray signed early comic work as Theophile Wagstaff, a joking persona of the author who wrote on snobs

explanation.surface: Amusing, in the manner of a Victorian satirist.
explanation.walkthrough: Thackeray wrote 'The Book of Snobs' and used joking pen-names, among them Theophile Wagstaff, hence the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular person is a wag, so playfully humorous behaviour is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Picture railway in poetic description

parts.note: a picture is an image

explanation.surface: A painting of a railway in poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative language in a poem, its metaphors and pictures, is called by this word.

clue.text: Writer (a jewel) has a degree in card-play

parts.note: beryl is a gemstone, the family that includes emerald
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A precious author holds a university degree in card games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' only links; the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl Bainbridge was an English novelist, so a writer.
